say.en: Every aluminium vessel in your kitchen was made by pushing electrons into molten alumina. Electrolysis runs a non-spontaneous reaction using an external source of electricity. In this lesson: State Faraday's two laws of electrolysis.
Calculate the mass deposited by a given charge.
Predict the products of electrolysis.

body.en: First law: the mass of substance deposited is proportional to the charge passed, m = ZIt. Second law: the same charge deposits masses proportional to their equivalent masses (molar mass ÷ electrons per ion). One faraday, F ≈ 96 500 C mol⁻¹, is the charge of one mole of electrons. So for Mⁿ⁺ + ne⁻ → M, n faradays deposit one mole of M.
body.kn: ಮೊದಲ ನಿಯಮ: ಕೂರುವ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಹರಿಸಿದ ವಿದ್ಯುದಾವೇಶಕ್ಕೆ ಅನುಪಾತ, m = ZIt. ಎರಡನೇ ನಿಯಮ: ಅದೇ ವಿದ್ಯುದಾವೇಶ ಸಮಾನ ತೂಕಗಳ ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿಯನ್ನು ಕೂರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಒಂದು ಫ್ಯಾರಡೇ ಸುಮಾರು 96500 ಕೂಲಂಬ್.

say.en: Moles of electrons equals Q over F.
M to the power n⁺ needs n F per mole of M.
In an electrolytic cell a battery drives a non-spontaneous reaction. Molten sodium chloride is the simplest case.
Sodium ions are reduced at the cathode; chloride ions are oxidised to chlorine at the anode.
Faraday's first law: the mass deposited is proportional to the charge passed.
Example: 2 amperes for 30 minutes through copper sulphate deposits 1.18 grams of copper.
In aqueous NaCl, water is reduced more easily than sodium ions, and chlorine forms at the anode because oxygen needs an overpotential.
Second law: the same charge deposits masses in the ratio of the equivalent masses.
On the board: electrolysis.

narration.en: Switch on the current. The mass deposited at the cathode is m = (I t / zF) × M: it grows with the current and the time, and for the same charge it depends on the molar mass and the charge on the ion.

body.en: The product depends on the electrolyte, the electrodes and the competing reactions at each electrode. Molten NaCl gives Na at the cathode and Cl₂ at the anode. Aqueous NaCl gives H₂ at the cathode (water is reduced more easily than Na⁺) and Cl₂ at the anode (O₂ needs a large overpotential). Dilute H₂SO₄ gives O₂ at the anode. With copper electrodes in CuSO₄, copper dissolves from the anode and deposits on the cathode, which is the basis of electrorefining.
body.kn: ಉತ್ಪನ್ನಗಳು ವಿದ್ಯುದ್ವಿಭಾಜ್ಯ, ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರೋಡ್ ಮತ್ತು ಸ್ಪರ್ಧಿಸುವ ಕ್ರಿಯೆಗಳನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸಿವೆ. ಜಲೀಯ NaCl ನಲ್ಲಿ ಕ್ಯಾಥೋಡ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ H₂ ಮತ್ತು ಆನೋಡ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ Cl₂ ದೊರೆಯುತ್ತವೆ.

problem.en: A CuSO₄ solution is electrolysed for 10 minutes with a current of 1.5 A. What mass of copper is deposited at the cathode? (Cu = 63.5 g mol⁻¹)

steps.en: Moles of electrons = 900/96 500 = 9.33 × 10⁻³ mol. Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu, so moles of Cu = 4.66 × 10⁻³ mol.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A CuSO₄ solution is electrolysed for 10 minutes with a current of 1.5 A. What mass of copper is deposited at the cathode? (Cu = 63.5 g mol⁻¹)

say.en: Let us solve this together. A CuSO 4 solution is electrolysed for 10 minutes with a current of 1.5 A. What mass of copper is deposited at the cathode? (Cu equals 63.5 grams mol to the power minus 1).
Q equals It equals 1.5 times 600 equals 900 C.
Moles of electrons equals 900 over 96 500 equals 9.33 times 10 to the power minus 3 moles. Cu squared⁺ plus 2e⁻ gives Cu, so moles of Cu equals 4.66 times 10 to the power minus 3 moles.
Mass equals 4.66 times 10 to the power minus 3 times 63.5 equals 0.296 grams.
So the answer is is approximately 0.296 grams of Cu.

problem.en: How long must a current of 5 A flow through CuSO₄ solution to deposit 1.27 g of copper?

steps.en: Moles of Cu = 1.27/63.5 = 0.02 mol; electrons needed = 2 × 0.02 = 0.04 mol.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. How long must a current of 5 A flow through CuSO₄ solution to deposit 1.27 g of copper?

say.en: Let us solve this together. How long must a current of 5 A flow through CuSO 4 solution to deposit 1.27 grams of copper?
Moles of Cu equals 1.27 over 63.5 equals 0.02 moles; electrons needed equals 2 times 0.02 equals 0.04 moles.
Charge Q equals 0.04 times 96 500 equals 3860 C.
t equals Q over I equals 3860 over 5 equals 772 seconds is approximately 12.9 minutes.
So the answer is 772 seconds about 12.9 minutes.

homework.en: How many coulombs are needed to reduce 1 mol of MnO₄⁻ to Mn²⁺?

narration.en: Recap. 1 F ≈ 96 500 C is the charge of one mole of electrons. Mass deposited m = MIt/(nF). Cells in series: moles deposited are in the inverse ratio of the charges on the ions. Aqueous NaCl gives H₂ at the cathode and Cl₂ at the anode.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಒಂದು ಫ್ಯಾರಡೇ ≈ 96500 C, ಒಂದು ಮೋಲ್ ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನುಗಳ ವಿದ್ಯುದಾವೇಶ. ಕೂರುವ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ m = MIt/(nF). ಸರಣಿಯಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಕೋಶಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಅದೇ ವಿದ್ಯುದಾವೇಶ ಹರಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಜಲೀಯ NaCl: ಕ್ಯಾಥೋಡ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ H₂, ಆನೋಡ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ Cl₂.

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. 1 F is approximately 96 500 C is the charge of one mole of electrons.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. ಒಂದು ಫ್ಯಾರಡೇ is approximately 96500 C, ಒಂದು ಮೋಲ್ ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನುಗಳ ವಿದ್ಯುದಾವೇಶ.

say.en: Mass deposited m equals MIt/nF.
Cells in series: moles deposited are in the inverse ratio of the charges on the ions.
Aqueous NaCl gives H 2 at the cathode and Cl 2 at the anode.
say.kn: ಜಲೀಯ NaCl: ಕ್ಯಾಥೋಡ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ H 2, ಆನೋಡ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ Cl 2.

say.en: Next: Batteries, fuel cells and corrosion.
